title: vector basics
concept: A vector is a dynamic array whose size is automatically adjusted.

steps.title: create vector
steps.explanation:
`vector<int> nums = {10, 20, 30}` creates a dynamic array containing 3 ints.

Internally, contiguous memory is allocated on the heap and the values ​​of the initialization list are copied.

steps.title: Add with push_back
steps.explanation:
`push_back(40)` adds a new element to the end of the array.

If capacity is sufficient, it is added immediately. If capacity is insufficient, larger memory is allocated and existing data is copied.

steps.title: Iterate and print
steps.explanation: Index access is possible like an array with `nums[i]`. `.size()` returns the current number of elements.

quiz.question: What is wrong with the description of vector?
options: O(1) access is possible by index.
quiz.explanation: push_back is usually O(1), and reallocation (O(n)) occurs only when capacity is exceeded. This is called amortized O(1).

misconceptions.wrong: vector is like a linked list
misconceptions.correct: A vector is a contiguous memory array and is a completely different data structure from a linked list.
misconceptions.why: Contiguous memory allows for high cache efficiency and O(1) index access.

keyTakeaway: Vectors are a convenient alternative to C arrays and handle size management and memory freeing automatically.
